verdict.rationale: CRA documents sanctioned third-party channels. Representatives request online access through the Represent a Client portal, businesses can authorize access to their online information, and EFILE-enrolled filers using certified software can file returns for clients. The evidence is mostly brief mentions, though, and EFILE is framed around individual T1 returns rather than business accounts. Missing for 10: detailed docs on how a business authorizes a representative (authorization levels, scope, revocation), explicit business-account coverage of the representative rail, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a legal-ops lead, the service documents a sanctioned third-party rail — designees, authorized providers, registered agents, or representatives — through which a provider can act for my company

citations.quote: representatives will need to use the Represent a Client portal to request online access to an account.
File a return or make a payment for an individual or business client
The sanctioned software-transmitter channel is EFILE: certified software plus an enrolled electronic filer transmit returns system-to-system
